### 14.11 CONTINUOUS TURN FUNCTION (OPTION)

#### 14.11.1 OVERVIEW

The continuous turn function (J613) allows continuous and limitless turn about the final robot axis or an additional turn axis of the robot in one direction. For example, this function is useful for rotating those devices that require continuous turn, such as conveyers, pumps, and grinders, about a robot axis or additional turn axis. The start and stop of continuous turn are directed from a program.

In normal operation, a robot axis is limited to a restricted number of turns from the zero position. An axis can only turn so far in one direction until the joint limit is reached and the axis must be unwound.

In continuous turn, there are no joint limits or turn limits. An axis can rotate indefinitely in the same direction without limitation. There is no absolute position of an axis beyond one turn. All positions of the continuous turn axis are mapped to the range [-180°, +180°]. For example, if an axis rotates 380 degrees, the position of the axis becomes 20 degrees.

Only a single continuous turn axis can be allocated for each motion group. The axis must satisfy the following conditions:

- Final axis of the robot
- Final axis of the positioner
- Final axis of integrated additional rotational axes
- Any auxiliary (non-integrated) additional rotational axes
- Final axis of the independent axes

The continuous turn axis must satisfy the following mechanical conditions:

- The mechanism must allow continuous operation (must be free of obstacles such as stoppers).
- The gear reduction ratio (value of Gear Ratio (motor) / Gear Ratio (axis) on the setting screen, the speed of the motor required for one turn about the axis) must be 4000 or less.

Note Gear Ratio (motor) and Gear Ratio (axis) means a ratio in an integer form that represents the amount of change of the axis position (angle displayed on the current position screen) by motor rotation. For example, if the axis position changes by 1 deg when the motor rotates 100 deg, Gear Ratio (motor) and Gear Ratio (axis) are as follows: Gear Ratio (motor) = 100, Gear Ratio (axis) = 1.

<!-- PDF page 1310 -->

### 14.11.1.1 MODES OF OPERATION

There are two modes of operation possible with the continuous turn option. They are:

- Constant velocity mode, also called the continuous rotation mode (CR).
- Non-continuous rotation mode (NCR).

#### 14.11.1.1.1 Continuous Rotation Mode

In the Continuous Rotation mode (CR), the axis rotates continuously at a specified velocity regardless of the motion of the other robot axes or auxiliary axes, except at the start and termination of continuous turn.

#### 14.11.1.1.2 Non-Continuous Rotation Mode

In the Non-Continuous Rotation mode (NCR), the continuous turn axis has position range within one turn and is coordinated with the other axes, but has no rotational limits.

When the axis moves, it will take the shortest rotational distance to the desired position.

### 14.11.1.2 FEATURES

In a standard FANUC America Corporation controller without continuous turn, the controlled axes are limited to a finite number of turns before a joint limit is reached. Without continuous turn, an axis cannot remain spinning while the rest of the robot completes a motion.

In a FANUC America Corporation robot controller that has the continuous turn option installed, the controlled axes are not limited in the number of turns they can make. A continuous turn axis will never reach a joint limit.

This section contains some of the other features included in the continuous turn option.

#### 14.11.1.2.1 Motor

The continuous turn option allows an axis to be treated as a motor rather than as a robot axis.

In the continuous rotation mode of operation, the desired velocity of the continuous turn axis is specified. This provides the capability of driving extended devices that require a motor drive, but also need to be coupled with the robot motion. Possible applications that might need this include conveyor drives, pump drives, grinders, sprayers, and so forth.

#### 14.11.1.2.2 Independence

The continuous rotation can be independent of robot motion but can also be synchronized with robot and group motion. The robot can stop while the continuous turn axis keeps spinning.

<!-- PDF page 1311 -->

# 14.11.1.2.3 No Rotational Limits

Another benefit is that the continuous turn axis can be stopped and indexed to different positions, without regard to rotational limits.

You can specify relative motions in which the desired position for the axis can be thousands of turns from the current position.

# 14.11.1.2.4 Shortest Distance

When this function is enabled in non-continuous rotation mode, turn is performed about the continuous turn axis from the current angle to the target angle in whichever direction incurs the least amount of motion. (Usually, the direction of turn about the axis is determined with the relationship between the current and target angles.) This the cycle time because the axis never needs to "unwind."

# 14.11.1.2.5 Mastering

Continuous turn maintains the axis mastering. The axis position is always correctly retained, even after continuous turn is disabled.

Re-mastering is not necessary even if you have rotated the axis for thousands of turns.

For more information on how to master a robot, refer to the appendix on "Mastering," in the appropriate controller-specific and application-specific FANUC America Corporation Setup and Operations Manual.

# 14.11.2 HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE

# 14.11.2.1 HARDWARE

Operating the Continuous Turn option requires the following hardware equipment:

# Robot

Continuous turn can run on the last axis of any FANUC America Corporation robot model that mechanically can support unlimited rotation of the last axis.

Refer to Section 14.11.9.1 for more information about gear ratios and supported robot models.

Extended axes are supported depending on their gear ratio and mechanical design.

# Memory

Continuous turn requires 30 KB of space in CMOS memory.

Continuous turn works independently of coprocessor speed.

<!-- PDF page 1312 -->

# Peripheral Devices

Continuous turn requires no additional peripheral devices but was designed for use with extended axes.

Note The only hardware limitations for continuous turn are the external cables and wires attached to the robot or extended axis. When designing your workcell to include continuous turn, make sure you consider the possibility of any external cables.

### 14.11.2.2 SOFTWARE

Continuous turn is an option for the core motion system.

Continuous turn can be loaded at Controlled Start to existing system software.

#### 14.11.2.2.1 Multi-Group Systems

In teach pendant programming, you can have multiple motion groups. However, you cannot specify the continuous turn velocity independently for each motion group. You can only specify the continuous turn velocity for all axes that have continuous turn enabled.

This means that when you execute group motion with continuous rotation, all groups with continuous turn will start to turn simultaneously, at the same velocity.

Also with multiple motion groups, the system variable:$MRR_GRP[i].$SV_OFF_ENB must be FALSE for each axis in all groups. This is a precautionary measure in case the first motion after a COLD START involves continuous turn. In this case there could be a synchronization problem between the motion groups when releasing the brakes and starting continuous rotation.

#### 14.11.2.2.2 Excluded Options

This function cannot be used together with the following functions:

- Asynchronous addition axis speed instruction. (The synchronous additional axis speed instruction can be used.)
- Arc sensor
- Weaving
- TCP speed estimation function (sealing flow rate control)
- Cannot use Incremental instruction (INC) for Continuous turn axis. (Can use only for non-continuous turn axis or the continuous turn axis is disabled case)Single and multiple motion group teach pendant programs without application programs

Note If continuous rotation is required, refer to Section 14.11.8 for an alternative method.

<!-- PDF page 1313 -->

### 14.11.3 GENERAL SETUP

#### 14.11.3.1 ENABLING CONTINUOUS TURN

This section contains the procedure for enabling continuous turn.

# **Procedure 14-21 Enabling Continuous Turn**

# **Conditions**

- The continuous turn option has been installed. Refer to the appropriate controller-specific *Software Installation Manual* for more information.

# **Steps**

1. Press MENU. The screen menu appears.
2. Select SETUP
3. Press F1, [TYPE]. The screen switching menu appears.
4. Select **Cont Turn**. The continuous turn setup screen appears.

SETUP Continuous Turn        G1      JOINT 10%
1: Group: 1
2: Continuous Turn Axis Num:   0
3: Gear Ratio (motor) :         0
4: Gear Ratio (axis)  :         0

# **Warning**

Never change continuous turn system variables outside of the setup menu. Bypassing the setup menu can corrupt the controller.

Table 14–21. Continuous Turn SETUP Screen Items

[tbl-300.md](tbl-300.md)

<!-- PDF page 1314 -->

[tbl-301.md](tbl-301.md)

# 5. Select Continuous Turn Axis Num:

This field indicates which axis in the group has continuous turn enabled. Setting "0" for Continuous Turn Axis Num.means continuous turn is completely disabled for the specified group.

6. Enter the robot axis number that you want to have continuous turn. Only the last axis of a robot or an extended axes can have continuous turn.

7. Select Gear Ratio (motor):

This field indicates the exact integer value of the numerator of the gear ratio for the continuous turn axis. This is the number of motor revolutions per revolutions of the joint specified in Gear Ratio (axis). The maximum value is 2147483646.

8. Select Gear Ratio (axis):

This field indicates the exact integer value of the denominator of the gear ratio for the continuous turn axis. This is the number of joint revolutions per revolutions of the motor specified in Gear Ratio (motor). The maximum value is 2147483646.

For the final robot axis, enter the “Group” and “Continuous Turn Axis Num”, and move the cursor to the “Gear Ratio (motor)” or “Gear Ratio (axis)”. Then F3, DEFAULT is displayed. Press F3, DEFAULT, then a message “Set gear ratio to the default values?” is displayed. Press F2, YES to set the Gear Ratio (motor) and Gear Ratio (axis).

Note F3, DEFAULT is not displayed in either of the following conditions:

- Software version is 7DF1/27(V9.10P/27), 7DF3/05(V9.30P/05) or earlier.
- Integrated additional axis, independent axis or positioner, etc. set by customers.

9. After completing the setup, press F4 DONE. The following message appears. "WARNING : Must COLD start to take effect."

10. Turn off the power, then turn it back on with a cold start.

### 14.11.3.2 MASTERING

The continuous turn option requires the exact gear ratio information in order to maintain mastering positions over all rotations.

<!-- PDF page 1315 -->

Additional mastering information is maintained during motion on the continuous turn axis. This additional information is kept in the "read-only" $DMR_GRP[i].$shift_error system variable.

### 14.11.3.2.1 Loss of Mastering Data

If you change any of the three system variable setup values during system setup, the additional mastering information, mentioned above, is cleared out. This means you could potentially lose mastering accuracy if the system variable setup values are changed after the initial continuous turn installation.

Even though the accuracy loss is less than one encoder pulse count, if you change the continuous turn setup frequently, the loss can accumulate.

# Warning

There is the potential of losing mastering data if you change the setup values for continuous turn frequently.

If accuracy is lost, re-mastering might be necessary.

For more information about how to master a robot, refer to the appendix on "Mastering," in the appropriate application-specific Setup and Operations Manual.

### 14.11.4 OPERATIONAL RULES

### 14.11.4.1 AXIS SETUP

The following axes and startup related rules must be applied when you operate continuous turn.

### 14.11.4.1.1 Only One Continuous Turn Axis

You are allowed one continuous turn axis per motion group. This implies that there can be up to three continuous turn axes on one controller; one per group.

When the motion group involves a robot with kinematics, only the last axis of the robot can be used as a continuous turn axis, provided that the mechanics of the robot permits it.

### 14.11.4.1.2 Auxiliary and Extended Axes

When the motion group involves auxiliary axes, any of the axes can be designated as the continuous turn axis.

If there are extended axes that are integrated, only the last extended axis can be used as a continuous turn axis.

<!-- PDF page 1316 -->

If the axes are non-integrated, any of the extended axes can be used provided there are no hardware limitations.

### 14.11.4.1.3 Configuration

The positional range of a continuous turn axis must be +/-180°.

Changing an axis to or from continuous turn can only be done on a Cold start.

When removing continuous turn from an axis, it is possible that the axis can be far outside the joint limits. You must first jog the axis back within the joint limits. The controller will only allow motion that returns the joint within the limits.

### 14.11.4.1.4 Gear Ratio

The maximum gear ratio allowed is 4000:1.

The maximum value of the numerator or denominator of the gear ratio is 2147483646.

Refer to Section 14.11.9.1 for more information about gear ratios.

### 14.11.4.1.5 UTOOL

When you use the robot axis for continuous rotation, the setting of $UTOOL should be such that there is no x or y component in the tool frame. Only z offsets are allowed.

Any other setting indicates that linear and circular motion will not be maintained when going from continuous rotation to non-continuous rotation.

If you set an incorrect or invalid continuous turn axis number, a warning message will be produced at Cold start.

In multiple groups, the $SV_OFF_ENBL system variable must be false for all groups. For example, brakes in groups that are coordinated through teach pendant programming, must not engage.

### 14.11.4.1.6 Mastering Data

With continuous turn installed and running, the mastering data for the continuous turn axis is automatically changed.

After continuous turn is installed, all off-line stored or written mastering data for the continuous turn axis is no longer valid. The robot will lose mastering on the continuous turn axis if these old numbers are re-installed. This includes saved system variables.

<!-- PDF page 1317 -->

### 14.11.4.2 STARTING AND STOPPING

The following operational rules must be applied when you start or terminate continuous turn motion.

#### 14.11.4.2.1 Acceleration

During continuous rotation mode, the acceleration of the continuous turn axis is specified by the following system variables:

- $PARAM_GROUP[i].$ACCEL_TIME1[contaxisnum]
- $PARAM_GROUP[i].$ACCEL_TIME2[contaxisnum]

The acceleration time will not change until the motion following continuous rotation.

During non-continuous rotation mode, the acceleration of the continuous turn axis is determined by the system variables $ACCEL_TIME1 and $ACCEL_TIME2 for joint motions, and $CART_ACCEL1 and $CART_ACCEL 2 for Cartesian motions.

These accelerations can be changed by the normal operation of the motion system, to speed up short motions. The short-motion speed-up in acceleration can be changed via $ACCEL_OVRD and $SHORTMO_MGN during joint motions.

#### Acceleration Switch

A switch, $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_grp_acc, is provided during continuous rotation mode, to ensure that all the axes in the group will have the same acceleration time as the continuous turn axis.

This switch can be changed only at Cold start.

#### 14.11.4.2.2 Deceleration

When you end continuous rotation, the continuous turn axis might rotate more than one turn as it smoothly decelerates to a stop. This depends on the acceleration times for the joint axis.

#### Speed

Robot motion might slow down during the ending motion, if the continuous turn axis becomes the speed limiting axis.

#### Synchronization

Synchronization with other groups and other axes in the same group, might be lost during the motion that ends continuous rotation.

<!-- PDF page 1318 -->

# 14.11.4.2.3 Moving to the Desired Position

When the robot goes to the desired position upon ending continuous rotation, the speed of the continuous turn axis will be calculated as the ratio of the robot motion speed over the maximum speedlim or speedjntim, depending on whether the motion was linear, circular, or joint.

When ending continuous rotation, the continuous turn axis will move to the desired position in the same direction as the continuous rotation. It will not "spin backwards." This feature is controlled by the system variable $CN_SAME_DIR, and can be disabled.

# 14.11.4.2.4 Ending Motion

The continuous turn option must be ended only on certain motions.

# Joint Motions

Continuous rotation must be ended on a joint motion if the continuous turn axis is the last axis of the robot. It can be ended on either a joint, linear, or circular motion if it is an extended axis.

# Relative Motions

Continuous rotation cannot be ended on a relative motion. The program is paused and an error message is posted.

# Process Motions

Continuous rotation cannot be ended on process motions. For example, continuous rotation cannot end on an Arc Start motion.

# 14.11.4.2.5 Recording Points

All points recorded while the continuous turn feature is enabled will be recorded in turn 0.

During playback of a previously recorded point that was not in turn 0, the desired position will be automatically wrapped into turn 0.

# 14.11.4.3 Speed

During continuous rotation, the rotational velocity is specified as a percentage of the maximum rotational velocity of the joint. This velocity is subject to teach pendant speed overrides and program overrides.

You can specify the continuous rotation axis speed indirectly by using a register. To use a register, press the F1, REGISTER, then type a register number.

<!-- PDF page 1319 -->

# 14.11.4.3.1 Limited by Mode of Operation

The maximum rotation velocity of a continuous turn axis is limited depending on the mode of operation.

Continuous Rotation: Limited by Maximum Axis Velocity (function of max motor speed and gear ratio).

Non-Continuous: Limited to 180 degrees per INTR loop.

All motion will stop and an error message will be issued if the program attempts to exceed the maximum speed during non-continuous rotation.

# 14.11.4.3.2 $CN_TURN_NO

$CN_TURN_NO is a system variable which shows the integral number of turns spun by an axis, since the start of continuous rotation. This variable is only valid for speeds under 1071 RPM for the joint. A warning message will be issued if the motion, without overrides, can exceed this speed.

Higher speeds are obtainable for the axis, but $CN_TURN_NO is not valid at these higher speeds.

# 14.11.4.4 MOTION

The following motion rules must be followed when you operate the continuous turn option.

# 14.11.4.4.1 FWD/BWD Single Step Motions

The system variable $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_step_enb acts as a switch by controlling CTV (continuous) motion when you single step through a program. You can change the value of this variable either on the teach pendant System Variables screen or in a KAREL program.

- When $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_step_enb = FALSE the continuous turn axis (in forward and backward single step motion), will not spin but will move the shortest rotational distance to the taught position.
- When $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_step_enb = TRUE the continuous turn axis does not move when in forward and backward single step mode.

Note After a PAUSE or SHIFT-RELEASE, pressing SHIFT and BWD causes the continuous turn axis to stay where it is for CTV motion.

<!-- PDF page 1320 -->

Table 14–22. $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_step_enb System Variable

[tbl-302.md](tbl-302.md)

Note The continuous turn system variable $CN_SAME_DIR, has no effect during forward (FWD) and backward (BWD) stepping.

### 14.11.4.4.2 Shortest Rotational Distance

When you move the robot to positions in non-continuous rotation mode, the continuous turn axis will move the shortest rotational distance.

Note If the continuous turn axis is the last axis of the robot, and the motion type is linear or circular, the robot motion type (linear/circular) takes precedence over the non-continuous rotation motion.

### 14.11.4.4.3 Jog

With continuous turn enabled, the selected axis can be jogged infinitely in either direction. The current position of the axis is displayed on either the CRT or teach pendant while jogging. The displayed position will wrap from +180 to -180 each time the axis crosses this boundary.

The continuous turn axis will move in non-continuous rotation mode during jogging.

In non-continuous rotation mode, the continuous turn axis can be jogged past 180°. The jog speed override is used when jogging.

### 14.11.4.4.4 Resume

On an operator panel HOLD or a teach pendant HOLD, the continuous turn axis will stop turning. It will resume turning when CYCLE START or SHIFT FWD are pressed only if the other axes in the group have a motion segment to resume.

If all other axes had completed their motion before HOLD was pressed, the continuous turn axis would not start turning until the next motion command.

<!-- PDF page 1321 -->

# 14.11.4.4.5 Positive Direction Bias

When you move the robot in the non-continuous rotation mode, 180° motions are biased towards rotation in the positive direction.

There is a small region of degrees, around 180°, where motions are biased to move in the positive direction. If the shortest rotational distance is greater then -179.99926°, then the axis will rotate in the positive direction rather than the negative direction.

For example, if the commanded rotation is 180.0°, the axis will rotate in the positive direction. If the commanded rotation is 180.00074°, the axis will still rotate in the positive direction, even though the shortest rotational distance is -179.99926°.

# 14.11.5 PROGRAMMING

You can only program continuous turn through the teach pendant editor. There are two modes of operation for continuous turn: continuous rotation, and non-continuous.

# Continuous

When operating in continuous rotation mode (CR), you must program the desired rotational velocity.

- In the teach pendant editor, you select a motion and attach an optional field for the continuous turn velocity called CTV

# Non-Continuous

When operating in non-continuous rotation mode (NCR), there are no special programming statements or commands to use the unrestricted joint motion feature of continuous turn.

# 14.11.5.1 TEACH PENDANT PROGRAMMING

This section discusses how to program continuous turn using the teach pendant editor.

The continuous rotation feature is located in the motion option page. You can add the continuous turn velocity option at the end of a motion line.

The default motion line is for no continuous rotation.

# Procedure 14-22 Adding Continuous Turn to a Motion Instruction

# Conditions

- All personnel and unnecessary equipment are out of the workcell.
- You want to add continuous turn velocity to the end of a motion instruction.

<!-- PDF page 1322 -->

- The program has been created and all detail information has been set correctly. If not, refer to "Planning and Creating a Program," in the application-specific FANUC America Corporation Setup and Operations Manual.

##### Steps

1. Press SELECT.
2. Select the program you want to modify.
3. Press EDIT.
4. Press and hold down the DEADMAN switch, while turning the teach pendant ON/OFF switch to ON.
5. Move the cursor to the end of the instruction for the line number of the motion instruction you want to modify. See the following screen for an example.

JOINT 10%
1: J P[1] 100% FINE

6. Press F4, [CHOICE]. You will see the following screen.

Motion Options
1: No option 5: Offset, Pr[]
2: ACC 6: Incremental
3: Skip, LBL[] 7: CTV
4: Offset 8:
1: J P[1] 100% FINE JOINT 10%

7. Select CTV. You will see a screen similar to the following.

JOINT 10%
1: J P[1] 100% FINE CTV

8. Enter a CTV option. Valid values range from -100 to +100. See the following screen for an example.

JOINT 10%
1: J P[1] 100% FINE CTV 50

<!-- PDF page 1323 -->

Note CTV0 means that the continuous turn axis does not rotate. However, CTV0 is treated as continuous rotation and must be ended as all other continuous rotation motions. When ending CTV0, the continuous turn axis will always take the shortest distance to the desired position.

When this option is added, continuous rotation at the specified velocity is turned on for the instruction. If there is no option, continuous rotation will be turned off automatically.

Note When you are in single STEP mode, CTV motions operate differently depending on the value of the system variable $CN_USR_GRP.$cn_step_enb.

# Continuous Termination Type

Continuous termination type is ignored on motions preceding the ending of continuous rotation. Example.

Ignore Continuous Termination Type Motions

--Robot will
stop at end of this
L P[2] 100mm/sec FINE
--motion, CONT100
is ignored.
L P[1] 100mm/sec CONT100 CTV100
--Robot will NOT stop since next
L P[2] 100mm/sec FINE CTV0
--motion, is a
continuous turn
L P[3] 100mm/sec FINE
--motion with
0 velocity.

#### 14.11.5.2 Programming Notes

# Note

- Continuous turn continues even if logic instructions (instructions other than those in operation statements) are executed.
- During program playback, the turn number for the continuous turn axis is ignored, and is always assumed to be "0."
- The turn number for the continuous turn axis at a point specified when this function is enabled is always stored as "0."

### 14.11.7 NOTES AND RESTRICTIONS

This function cannot be used together with the following functions:

- TAST
- Weaving
- TCP Speed Prediction function (sealing flow rate control)
- TCP Speed Output
- Coordinated Motion (You can use together with this function if you set up the Continuous Rotation axis in other than coordinated motion groups and use programs with separate group mask.

If the software version is 7DF1/16 (V9.10P/16) or earlier, Continuous Rotation function is not available with SR-3iA and SR-6iA series.

Note the following when using this function:

<!-- PDF page 1326 -->

- When this function is disabled, the current position on the continuous turn axis may fall outside the stroke limits. If this occurs, move the position on continuous turn axis within the stroke limits using jog feed or a program.
- If, on a multi-group system, the settings on the SETUP Continuous Turn screen are changed and the F4 DONE key is pressed, it is necessary to set system variable $PARAM_GROUP[group].$SV_OFF_ENB[i] (where i is an axis number) to FALSE to disable break control for all the axes for all operation groups before turning the power back on with a cold start.
- On a multi-group system, even if there are multiple continuous turn axes, separate continuous turn speeds cannot be specified for them.
- Original Path Resume feature is disabled when continuous turn loaded. Even if system variable ($SCR.$ORG_PTH_RSM) set enabled, feature is disabled when cycle power.
- If continuous turn axis is in any of the motion groups, Cycle Time Priority feature for Cartesian motion and Constant Path feature are disabled in all groups.

— If Cycle Time Priority feature for Cartesian motion is disabled, the cycle time is possible to be longer.

— If Constant Path feature is disabled in servogun system, alarm

- Following setup allows Cycle Time Priority feature for Cartesian motion and Constant Path feature to work in those motion groups that DOES NOT involve

1. Set bit 22 of $SCR.$UPDATE_MAP1 = TRUE
2. Set $SCR_GRP[g].$USE_TBCART = TRUE
3. Set $GROUP[g].$CARTFLTRENB = TRUE
4. Set $CPCFG.$CP_ENABLE = TRUE (Default TRUE)
5. Reset bit 0, bit 4 and bit 10 of $SCR.$MB_DSBL_MSK = False [ Example 2 ].
6. If $SGSYSCFG.$LIN_DST_ENB and $SGSYSCFG.$LIN_DST_ENB are changed for SVGN-149 countermeasure, reset TRUE.
7. Cycle power.

### 14.11.8 SPECIAL KAREL REMASTERING PROGRAM FOR HANDLING CONTINUOUS ROTATING AXES

Note This program is loaded with the Continuous Turn Option. However, the program can be used only for axes that do not or cannot be set up as Continuous Turn Axes.

From software version V8.30P/31, the continuous rotation function provides a KAREL "CALIBNBT.PC" which can reset the number of rotation. For example, in case of coordinated motion of robot with positioner and rotating positioner one direction continuously, use CALIBNBT.PC instead; because continuous rotation function is not available in this case. By using CALIBNBT.PC, motion group except for robot (such as a positioner or an independent axis) can reset the position of its own rotational axis within +-180[deg].

<!-- PDF page 1327 -->

##### 14.11.8.1 Condition to Use

When the following conditions are all satisfied, you can use CALIBNBT.PC.

- Target axis does not belong to robot group (such as a positioner or an independent axis)
- Mastering is already done at correct position before using CALIBNBT.PC
- Absolute number of upper and lower stroke limits of axis which will be reset is smaller than below equation

> **Image description -- img-106.jpeg:** The image contains a diagram and a mathematical example related to motor rotation limits and gear ratios. The diagram shows a relationship between motor revolutions (motor rev) and axis revolutions (axis rev), with a label indicating 'motor rotation limit' and 'angle of one rotation [deg]'. The gear ratio is represented as a fraction with 4085 in the numerator and the gear ratio in the denominator. The angle of one rotation in degrees is calculated as 360 divided by the gear ratio. The example provided calculates the angle of one rotation for a gear ratio of 100: 360 / 100 = 4.085 degrees. It then states that the axis limit must be greater than -14706 degrees and less than 14706 degrees, derived from the motor rotation limit of 4085 multiplied by the angle of one rotation (4.085 degrees). The diagram and text together explain how to determine the permissible axis rotation limits based on the motor's rotation limit and gear ratio.

Note Please confirm the following:

- When the pulse count of one axis rotation is not an integer, position error after the decimal point is accumulated at rotation reset.

> **Image description -- img-107.jpeg:** The image contains a mathematical formula and an example calculation related to the pulse count of a motor and its axis. The formula states: 'Pulse count of axis one rotation = gear ratio x 2^23'. Below the formula, an example is provided: 'Example: Suppose gear ratio = 2763/16'. The calculation follows: '2763/16 x 2^23 = 90537984'. The text also mentions that this results in an 'integer and no position error'. The formula and example illustrate how the pulse count for one full rotation of an axis is derived by multiplying the gear ratio by 2 raised to the power of 23.

- To clear the error of position, execute mastering of the axis periodically. (If it is integer, mastering is no need)
- Please execute CALIBNBT.PC while robot stays stationary. If executing CALIBNBT.PC after motion sentence, please execute after FINE term-type motion. (Do not execute during CNT motion)
- At calling CALIBNBT.PC program, the number of rotation is reset to set current position within +-180 [deg].
- If current position is within +-180 [deg], CALIBNBT.PC program does nothing.

##### 14.11.8.2 Usage

Set the following two system variables.

- $PARAM2_GRP[group].$GRATIO_DIV[axis] : Gear Ratio (motor)
- $PARAM2_GRP[group].$GRATIO_NUM[axis] : Gear Ratio (axis)

For the robots and FANUC's positioners, these values are preset and do not need to be changed. If the software version is 7DF1/27 (V9.10P/27), 7DF3/05 (V9.30P/05) or earlier, these system variables do not need to be set (the setting has no effect).

<!-- PDF page 1328 -->

Note If the above-mentioned system variables for the Gear Ratio (motor) and Gear Ratio (axis) are set and when you execute a mastering of this axis after using CALIBNBT.PC, set the following system variable to 0: $DMR_GRP[group].$REL_SHF_ERR[axis].$OFFSET[axis]

Use CALIBNBT.PC according to below usage.

- Set $KAREL_ENB = 1 to display KAREL in program list menu.
- Use CALL instruction of teach program to execute CALIBNBT.PC.

Note When DCS Position / Speed Check function is enabled, you cannot use CALIBNBT.PC. If you call CALIBNBT.PC when DCS Position / Speed Check function is enabled, an alarm "SYST-212 Need to apply to DCS param" occurs. If you need to use CALIBNBT.PC, disable Dual Check Safety function by setting $DCS_CFG.$EXCLUDE[Group number] to -1.

- Assign two arguments as below to call CALIBNBT.PC CALIBNBT ( group number , axis number ) Argument 1 : group number 1 to 8 Argument 2 : axis number 1 to 9 ex ) To reset turn number of group 2 / axis 1. CALL CALIBNBT (2, 1)
- If the axis is dual drive axis, please assign the number of axis of master group.

### 14.11.10 SPIRAL CLADDING

### 14.11.10.1 Overview

In general, the motion direction (from P2 to P3) is parallel to the continuous turn axis, so the equation that computes the total pitch distance is correct by projecting the robot motion vector to the pitch direction. The spiral cladding is different in that the robot motion direction (from P2 to P3) is perpendicular to the continuous turn axis, as depicted in the following figure.

<!-- PDF page 1341 -->

Figure 14-41.

> **Image description -- img-108.jpeg:** The image depicts a robotic arm in a manufacturing or assembly setting. The arm is positioned above a curved, yellow component, likely a car body panel, with a visible label indicating a 'Continuous Path Axis Decision' and 'Motion Direction'. The robotic arm appears to be equipped with a tool or end effector, possibly for welding, painting, or assembly tasks. In the top-right corner, there is a user interface window displaying a program or script labeled 'TEST2' with multiple lines of code. The code includes commands such as 'SP[1] 20% FINE', 'CALL CNV_CTR(10,1,1)', and 'MOVL P[2] 150mm/sec FINE', suggesting instructions for the robotic arm's movement and operation. The interface also shows a status bar with options like 'Edit', 'Online', 'Monitor', and 'Remote'. The overall scene indicates a controlled, automated process involving precise robotic manipulation.

When the robot's direction of traveling is perpendicular to the continuous turn axis, the total pitch distance in (eq. 1) becomes 0 and the robot traveling speed (eq. 2) becomes very large. In order to handling the new requirements, the CN_CTS call now has a third argument, as shown in the picture above. The third argument is optional, if this argument is not specified or set to 0, the continuous turn speed control software will assume the motion direction is parallel to the continuous turn axis. If the third argument is specified and non-zero, then the continuous turn speed control assumes the motion direction is perpendicular to the continuous turn axis and compute the robot motion speed accordingly.

When the third argument in CN_CTS is specified and non-zero, the first parameter, the pitch distance, is specified in the direction of robot motion that is perpendicular to the continuous turn axis. Special cases: Since the continuous turn speed control also supports conic section, that is, the robot motion may not always parallel to the continuous turn axis. The continuous turn speed control allows the robot motion to move from 0 degree (parallel to the continuous turn axis) to +- 84 degree. If the slope of the motion exceeds the constraint, the continuous turn axis will automatically switch its algorithm to use the perpendicular method when it detects the condition even the user did not specify the third argument in the CN_CTS call.

#### 14.11.10.2 Multiple Group Support

The CTS software determines the continuous turn group based on the program group mask and the setting of the continuous turn axis. However, if a system has a robot that works with two or more continuous turn groups, and in some cases, the CTS cannot determine the correct continuous turn groups, a 4th argument can be used to specify the continuous turn axis's group number.

<!-- PDF page 1342 -->

For example, a system is set up with robot in group 1 and continuous turn axis on group 2 and group 3. The user has created a TP program to work group 1 and group 2, and another TP program for group 1 and group 3. Each individual TP program works fine. When the user creates a JOB program that call both programs, and the Job program has group mask for all three groups. When the CALL CN_CTS is executed, the CTS will post an error since it does not know which group the CN_CTS should apply to due to the program mask has all three groups.

This problem can be eliminated by setting the JOB program with no group mask, or the user can program the continuous turn with the 4th argument: CALL CN_CTS(10, 1, 0, 2) << the 4th argument indicates the CN_CTS call should apply to group 2 continuous turn axis. The 4th argument is optional and, if not specified, the CTS will determine the correct continuous turn group as before.

### 14.12 COORDINATES OFFSET FUNCTION

#### 14.12.1 Using the Coordinates Offset Function

The coordinates offset function changes either the tool coordinate system or the user coordinate system for a range of motion instructions in a program for which teaching has been completed. The function then converts the positional data so that the TCP position does not change due to the shift between the original and changed coordinate systems.

**Types of Coordinates Offset**

The following two kinds of coordinates offset are available:

- TOOL OFFSET - Changes the **tool** coordinate system number and positional data in a teach pendant program.
- UFRAME OFFSET - Changes the **user** coordinate system number for the positional data in a teach pendant program.

Coordinates offset is executed on the TOOL/UFRAME OFFSET screens (UTILITIES, Tool offset/Frame offset). The screens are switched as shown in Figure 14–42.

<!-- PDF page 1343 -->

Figure 14–42. Coordinates Offset Screens

> **Image description -- img-109.jpeg:** The image is a flowchart diagram illustrating the navigation between two screens in a program: the "Program name setting screen" and the "Coordinate system number setting screen." The diagram shows that pressing the key combination SHIFT + '+' on the "Program name setting screen" navigates to the "Coordinate system number setting screen." Conversely, pressing SHIFT + '+' on the "Coordinate system number setting screen" returns to the "Program name setting screen." Additionally, pressing the F2 key followed by the EXECUTE key on the "Coordinate system number setting screen" executes a change or shift operation. The arrows indicate the direction of navigation or action between the screens.

### Coordinates Offset

The coordinates offset function performs the following:

- Changes the tool coordinate system number or user coordinate system number for the positional data (Cartesian coordinates) in all or a range of motion instructions in an existing program.
- If the positional data is specified with joint coordinates, converts the data according to the shift resulting from the tool or user coordinate system change.
- Inserts the results of the conversion into a new or existing program.
- Executes the same conversion for other programs, if necessary.

### Converting the Positional Data

The positional data is converted according to the following rules:

### Position and attitude

- Positional data specified with Cartesian coordinates is converted to Cartesian coordinates. Positional data specified with joint coordinates is converted to joint coordinates.
- If the converted joint coordinates fall outside the operating range, the corresponding positional data is assumed to be untaught. For Cartesian coordinates, the converted position is stored as is.
- The positional data in the position registers is not converted.
- For motion instructions that include the incremental motion option, positional data specified with joint coordinates is assumed to be untaught.

Axis location and rotation speed of positional data specified with Cartesian coordinates

- The same format is used both before and after conversion.

<!-- PDF page 1344 -->

- If the wrist axis is rotated through  \( 180^{\circ} \)  or more as a result of conversion, the rotation speed for the axis is optimized; a message is then displayed prompting you to select whether to use the optimized rotation speed.

For UTOOL OFFSET, you can select either of the following positional data conversion methods:

- TCP fixed: This method lets you specify a new TOOL frame number of your choice for use with a new or damaged tool. Programmed positions are not changed. The same TCP path will be maintained with this new UTOOL, but the faceplate position will be different. See Figure 14–43.

Figure 14-43. TCP Fixed Method

It shows two programs: the Original Program (left) using UTOOL: 1 and the Offset Program (right) using UTOOL: 2. Both programs have identical motion instructions for points P[1], P[2], and P[3] with a speed of 50 mm/sec and a fine termination. The diagram highlights the robot's TCP path for the old tool (dashed line) and the new tool (solid line). The diagram emphasizes that the robot's movement path (TCP path) is preserved, but the tool's orientation and position are adjusted based on the selected UTOOL.

### 14.13 CRW SHAPE GENERATION

#### 14.13.1 Overview

This function makes it easy to create machining programs aimed at welding 2-dimensional shapes (hereinafter called welding shape program) using a Compact Remote Welder (hereinafter called CRW). The guide screen of the CRW Shape Generation Function is added to iHMI, and it enables creating a welding shape program via a step-by-step sequence.

### 14.13.3 Execution of a Welding Shape Program

Welding shape programs generated by CRW Shape Generation function have a motion group of CRW only. So, welding shape programs need to be executed by a production program (main program) with a CALL instruction or a RUN instruction, depending on the application.

Warning

Ensure that the calling sequence of the welding shape program for proper processing is performed correctly.

When an error occurs, check to stop the welding process. The CRW Shape Generation function does not automatically stop the machining process. Design the system such that the machining process is properly stopped when an error occurs. Otherwise, machining processes that are not stopped properly can harm workers or peripheral devices.

### 14.13.3.1 Execution of a Point Welding Shape Program

When a point welding shape is selected and a welding shape program is generated, laser welding is performed without robot motion.

Figure 14–50. Execution of a Point Welding Shape Program

> **Image description -- img-124.jpeg:** The diagram illustrates the execution order between two programs, MAIN.TP and CRW_PROG.TP. MAIN.TP contains three lines of code, with line 2 showing a call to CRW_PROG (highlighted in blue). CRW_PROG.TP contains three lines of code: line 1 defines a shape as a generated circle, line 2 sets the tool number to 1, and line 3 sets the frame number to 0. Blue arrows indicate the flow of execution from line 2 of MAIN.TP to CRW_PROG.TP, showing that CRW_PROG is called and executed in sequence. The diagram visually represents the control flow and interaction between the two programs.

Therefore, the welding shape program must be executed by the main program with a CALL instruction as shown below.

### 14.13.3.2 Execution of a Path Welding Shape Program

When a path welding shape is selected and a welding shape program is generated, laser welding is performed with robot motion.

Therefore, a welding shape program must be executed by the main program with a RUN instruction as shown below.

<!-- PDF page 1358 -->

Figure 14–51. Execution of a Path Welding Shape Program

> **Image description -- img-125.jpeg:** The diagram shows the execution order of two task programs, MAIN.TP and CRW_PROG.TP. MAIN.TP contains three lines of code: line 1 is empty, line 2 calls the subroutine 'RUN CRW_PROG', and line 3 is empty. CRW_PROG.TP contains three lines of code: line 1 is a comment '!SHAPE GENERATED WOBBLING', line 2 sets the variable 'UTOOL_NUM' to 1, and line 3 sets the variable 'UFRAME_NUM' to 0. An arrow labeled 'Execution order' points from line 2 of MAIN.TP to line 1 of CRW_PROG.TP, indicating that the 'RUN CRW_PROG' command in MAIN.TP triggers the execution of CRW_PROG.TP. The diagram also notes that CRW_PROG.TP is part of another task.

Note When a path welding shape is selected, the generated welding shape program continues welding until R[1] becomes 1. Therefore, please modify the welding shape program and change the end condition of welding appropriately.

(It is assumed that the main program executes and stops the execution of the path welding shape program. Therefore, please put the instruction that matches the end condition in the main program.)

### 14.14 CYCLE TIME LOGGING AND DISPLAY

#### 14.14.1 Overview

The Cycle Time Logging and Display function allows you to track and display teach pendant program cycle times. Cycle times are tracked based on individual cycles and hourly averages. Multiple cycles can be observed to view trends and analyze data.

Typically, the iPendant is used to display the cycle time data graphically. However, raw cycle time data can also be observed.

By default the cycle time is tracked from the start of a teach pendant program until the program ends. However, you can adjust this by adjusting the $CY_CONFIG system variable.

The tracked cycle time is based on multiple categories. See Table 14–28. Table 14–29 lists the items displayed on the Cycle Time Display screen.

### 14.14.2.3 Line by Line Mode

If the $lineenable=TRUE and $numlines>0, line-by-line cycle time tracking will be enabled. This allows you to track a defined number of lines in the current program. This information is stored in cycline.dg on DRAM and is lost when the controller is turned off. This file can only be viewed using the Web Server or by selecting Line Text from the [PAGE] function key.

### 14.14.3 Tracking Cycle Time

Procedure 14-26 Tracking Cycle Time on the iPendant

Conditions

- You are using an iPendant to display the cycle time data graphically.
- The program you want to track has been executed at least one time.

1. Press MENU.
2. Select STATUS.
3. Press F1, [TYPE].
4. Select Cycle Time.

<!-- PDF page 1364 -->

5. Set the name of the program for which you want cycle time data displayed. By default, ALL programs are selected. To select a single program to display, press F2, [PROG], and select the name of the program.
6. To change the cycle time display between cycles and hours, press F3, [ZOOM] and select the kind of information you want displayed. After you have made a display selection (cycles or hours) you can quickly change the display by using the arrow keys. The up and down arrow keys move from one cycle or hour to ten cycles or hours, then a hundred cycles or hours. The left and right arrow keys can move forward or backward through the cycles or hours. To move forward or backward quickly, press SHIFT and the left or right arrow key. If you are in ten cycle mode it will 5. If you are in ten cycle mode, it will move the display by 30.

7. If you want to change the way the cycle time information is displayed, press F2, [PAGE], and select one of the following:

- Cycle graphics which displays the cycle time information graphically on the iPendant.
- Cycle text which displays the raw cycle text information. The cycle information is stored in CYCLES.DG.
- Average text which displays the average raw cycle text information. The average text information is stored in CYCAVE.DG.
- Line text which displays the line by line raw text information. This information is stored in CYCLINE.DG.

Note All of this information can be displayed from the web server.

8. To display cycle time information for a specific program category, press F4, [CATGRY], and then select the category of information you want displayed.
9. To change whether the cycle time information is displayed graphically or as raw text, press >, NEXT, press F2, [PAGE], and then select the kind of display you want.
10. To clear the current cycle or hourly data, press >, NEXT, and then press F3, [UPDATE]. Select Clear Cycle Data which clears all cycle information.

Note You might want to clear the current cycle or hourly data if you are done tracking it and you want to start over, or if you want to load historical data and do not want to compare it with what currently exists on the controller.

11. To load preexisting cycle data, press >, NEXT, press F3, [UPDATE], then select Load Cycle Data.
12. To begin collecting hourly data, press >, NEXT, press F3, [UPDATE], then select Collect Hourly Data.
13. To enable line by line cycle time tracking, you must set the following system variables: $CY_CONFIG.$LINEENABLE=TRUE and $NUMLINES=number of lines to track. After the system variables are set, you must update the line by line information.
14. If you want to set a target cycle time which will be displayed as a horizontal gold bar when one cycle is displayed,

- Press SELECT and select the current program.

<!-- PDF page 1365 -->

- Press >, NEXT, and then press F2, DETAIL.
- Press F3, NEXT until Target Cycle Time(seconds) is displayed.
- Press ENTER and type a new target cycle time.
- When you have finished, press F1, END, and then press ENTER.
- Press MENU, select STATUS, press F1, [TYPE] and select Cycle Time if it is not already displayed.
- Press >, NEXT, and then press F2, [PROG] to select the current program.
- Press F3, [ZOOM], and select One Cycle. You will see a screen similar to the following.

Figure 14–56. Target Cycle Time

### 14.15 DATA MONITOR

#### 14.15.1 Overview

Data Monitor is a tool for improving process quality. You can use it to monitor and record important process parameters. It can alert you to a parameter going out of limit and it can record data for use in a quality record.

Data Monitor operates much like a strip chart recorder or a data acquisition system. To use the Data Monitor feature you make selections in two or three teach pendant screens (depending what application you are using). Specifically,

<!-- PDF page 1367 -->

- Enable or disable any specific features in the Data Monitor Utility screen
- Select items to monitor (such as arc current feedback or actual flow rate) with one of the Data Monitor schedules

You can monitor up to 11 items at once with a Data Monitor schedule. The maximum sampling frequency is 250 Hz. You can specify separate frequencies for limit checking and for recording. As the items specified in the schedule are recorded, the following data is also collected: time, date, distance, program name and line number. You can choose the items you want to monitor from the Data Monitor Schedule screen.

As data is recorded, it can be formatted as a report and sent to a file.

A short example report is shown in Report Example. The data is tab-delimited for importing into a spreadsheet application.

Report Example

[tbl-326.md](tbl-326.md)

##### Definitions

This section contains definitions of terms you should know to use Data Monitor.

Item - A specific data element to be monitored. For example, an I/O signal, like WO[2] (for ArcTool) or DO[2] (for PaintTool or DispenseTool) or AI[2]. Data Monitor can monitor the following kinds of items:

• System variables (Real or Integer only)
• KAREL program variables (Real or Integer only)
• I/O ports (digital and analog)

Schedule -A set of parameters that define how to monitor specific items and where to save recorded data.

<!-- PDF page 1368 -->

Trigger - A condition that must be met to begin or end monitoring.

Limit - A defined high or low value for a monitored item.

# Monitoring Limits

The monitoring option can check each sampled data item against upper and lower boundary limits. If the sampled data value is past a limit for a specified time period an alarm occurs. You must specify two upper and two lower limits for each monitored data item. See Figure 14–58.

Figure 14–58. Process Limits

> **Image description -- img-132.jpeg:** The image is a time-series graph illustrating operational thresholds and warning states over time. The horizontal axis represents time, while the vertical axis represents different operational states or thresholds. The graph includes the following labeled lines: Upper Pause, Upper Warn, Nominal, Lower Warn, and Lower Pause. A solid line fluctuates within these thresholds over time, indicating the system's operational state. Key annotations include: 'OK' indicating the system is within nominal bounds, 'T_min' marking minimum time intervals between state transitions, and 'Warn' indicating a warning state when the system approaches or exceeds the Upper Warn or Lower Warn thresholds. The graph shows the system transitioning from the nominal state to warning states (Upper Warn or Lower Warn) and eventually to pause states (Upper Pause or Lower Pause) if the conditions persist or worsen. The relationships depicted show how the system's state changes over time in response to certain conditions, with the solid line representing the system's operational trajectory relative to the defined thresholds.

One limit is of a WARN severity. If the first limit is crossed for a specified time a digital output is set to ON, but normal operation continues. If the monitored process signal returns to an acceptable value for a specified time or if sampling ends, the digital output is turned OFF. The second limit is more severe and has a PAUSE severity. If the second limit is crossed for the specified time, a pause error is posted immediately and the same digital output is set to ON. The digital output is set OFF if:

- The teach pendant program is resumed.
- The teach pendant program is aborted.
- The system is RESET.

# Procedure 14-27 Setting Up Data Monitor

# Conditions

• Data Monitor is installed on your controller.

# Steps

1. Press MENU.
